scope: Theorem 9.1 (Constant cohomology) of the manuscript “Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes” (preprints/Filtered-chromatic-splitting-at-generic-primes-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f2aeefc98af1afcd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For G = Ka, Ia, or Pa, the groups Hq(G, Zp) are finite free Zp-modules, vanish for q > a2, and have Poincaré polynomial X q rankZp Hq (G, Zp)zq = a Y i=1 (1 + z2i−1 ). (9.1) There are exterior-algebra presentations over Zp, and over every finite extension of Fp, with generators in degrees 2i − 1, 1 ≤ i ≤ a. For every r ≥ 1, reduction induces an isomorphism Hq (G, Zp)/pr ∼ − − → Hq (G, Z/pr ). (9.2) The actual restriction maps H∗ (Ka, Zp) −→ H∗ (Ia, Zp), H∗ (Ka, Z/pr ) −→ H∗ (Ia, Z/pr ) are isomorphisms. These assertions do not select the generators: the compatible stable generators will be constructed in Theorem 10.1.
